hfaqs.a: No. Start with spoken Marathi in Roman letters, and let Devanagari come second. Learners who speak first stay motivated far longer than learners who drill letters for a month before saying a word.
hfaqs.q: Must I learn Devanagari before speaking?

hfaqs.a: नमस्कार for respect, हो and नाही, धन्यवाद, माफ करा, ठीक आहे, and मी — I. With those seven you can open any interaction in Maharashtra politely while your vocabulary grows underneath.
hfaqs.q: Which words should I learn in week one?

hfaqs.a: The rolled ळ, nasal vowels, and three-gender verbs — जातो, जाते, जातं. Ten minutes of daily listening retunes your ears within weeks; the pronunciation page walks you through each sound.
hfaqs.q: What is the hardest part of Marathi?

Each phrase speaks in a native Marathi voice. Slow it to 0.2× and repeat until it sticks.
Every topic ends in practice: quiz yourself, then review the words until they stay.

title: Marathi

topics.desc: नमस्कार and beyond — greet Maharashtra with warmth from your first word. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: नमस्कार with folded hands — respectful everywhere, from Mumbai locals to village homes. Informal राम राम works with friends; नमस्कार never fails.
faqs.q: How do I say hello respectfully?

faqs.a: तुम्ही कसे आहात? (formal) or तू कसा आहेस? (informal) — and answer मी ठीक आहे, धन्यवाद (I'm fine, thanks). Health-questions open Marathi hearts.
faqs.q: How do I ask how someone is?

faqs.a: शुभ सकाळ (good morning), शुभ दुपार (good afternoon), शुभ संध्याकाळ (good evening), शुभ रात्री (good night). Time-greetings show care; use them generously.

topics.lede: नमस्कार and beyond — greet Maharashtra with warmth from your first word.
topics.note: A note on नमस्कार. नमस्कार (namaskar — I bow to you) carries folded hands and genuine warmth — Maharashtra's universal key. Say it to auto drivers, CEOs and grandmothers alike; the returned smile is guaranteed. Respect first, everything else follows.
paras: Greetings open every door: नमस्कार (respectful hello), राम राम (informal hello), हाय (casual hi). Fold your hands, say नमस्कार, and Maharashtra opens — buses, bazaars, boardrooms. One word, infinite welcome.

Health-questions show you care: तुम्ही कसे आहात? (how are you, formal), मी ठीक आहे (I'm fine), आणि तुम्ही? (and you?). Marathi small talk runs on genuine enquiry — ask properly, listen properly, belong quickly.

Time splits the day: शुभ सकाळ (good morning), शुभ दुपार (good afternoon), शुभ संध्याकाळ (good evening), शुभ रात्री (good night). Morning greetings before noon, रात्री only at parting — timing your शुभ shows cultural fluency.

Partings promise return: निरोप (farewell), पुन्हा भेटू (we'll meet again), काळजी घ्या (take care). Marathis rarely say goodbye without a next meeting — पुन्हा भेटू assumes friendship continues. Say it warmly; mean it always.
topics.title: Saying hello the Marathi way

topics.desc: Devanagari plus ळ — vowels, consonants and barakhadi, made friendly. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Nearly — Marathi uses Devanagari like Hindi, plus ळ (retroflex lla) and a few combined letters. Hindi readers start Marathi script at eighty percent.
faqs.q: Is Marathi script the same as Hindi?

faqs.a: The vowel-consonant grid: क का कि की कु कू... Every consonant marries every vowel in order. Master one row fully and the whole grid unlocks.
Vowels first: अ आ इ ई उ ऊ ए ऐ ओ औ — then क ख ग घ च छ ज झ. Sounds before shapes; reading follows speaking.

topics.lede: Devanagari plus ळ — vowels, consonants and barakhadi, made friendly.

links.desc: Letters from zero, step by step.
links.label: Marathi basics

topics.note: A note on ळ. ळ (lla — retroflex L) is Marathi's signature sound — बाळ (child), माळ (garland), काळ (time). Curl the tongue back and let it flap forward. Hindi lacks it; Marathi flaunts it. Master ळ and natives grin with delight.
paras: Vowels anchor everything: अ आ इ ई उ ऊ ए ऐ ओ औ अं अः — thirteen pure sounds. Long-short pairs matter — इ vs ई changes meaning. Chant them in order daily; the mouth memorises what the ear repeats.

Consonants march in families: क ख ग घ (throat), च छ ज झ (palate), ट ठ ड ढ (roof), त थ द ध (teeth), प फ ब भ (lips). Family by family, feel where each sound lives — Marathi pronunciation is geography you can touch.

Special letters crown the set: य र ल व श ष स ह ळ क्ष ज्ञ — with ळ (retroflex L) and ज्ञ as Marathi treasures. शाळा (school) shows ळ in action; ज्ञान (knowledge) shows ज्ञ. Special letters, everyday words.

Barakhadi grids it all: क का कि की कु कू के कै को कौ कं कः — each consonant through every vowel. One grid mastered teaches all grids. Read barakhadi aloud for a month; Devanagari becomes a friend for life.
topics.title: Marathi alphabet

topics.desc: एक दोन तीन to शंभर — count, pay and bargain in Marathi. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: एक दोन तीन चार पाच सहा सात आठ नऊ दहा — chant to ten, then अकरा बारा तेरा... to twenty. Rhythm first, precision follows.
वीस (20), तीस (30), चाळीस (40), पन्नास (50) — then combine: एकवीस (21), बत्तीस (32). Tens plus units, endlessly.
शंभर (100), हजार (1000), लाख (100,000). किती? (how many?) asks; numbers answer. Markets run on these three.

topics.lede: एक दोन तीन to शंभर — count, pay and bargain in Marathi.
topics.note: A note on किती? किती? (kiti — how much / how many?) is Maharashtra's most useful question — किती रुपये? (how many rupees?), किती वाजले? (what time is it?). One word, every transaction. Ask किती fearlessly; numbers come to you.
paras: One to ten sings: एक दोन तीन चार पाच सहा सात आठ नऊ दहा — chant it walking, cooking, waiting. Marathi numbers love rhythm; your tongue learns faster than your brain. Ten numbers, total freedom in every shop.
Teens climb steadily: अकरा बारा तेरा चौदा पंधरा सोळा सतरा अठरा एकोणवीस वीस — eleven to twenty. एकोणवीस (19) and वीस (20) open the tens; climb daily and teens become trivial.

Tens multiply power: वीस तीस चाळीस पन्नास साठ सत्तर ऐंशी नव्वद शंभर — 20 to 100. Combine freely: एकवीस (21), पंचवीस (25), त्र्याऐंशी... practise सत्तावीस (27) and अडतीस (38) — the tongue-twisters that prove fluency.
Hundreds rule markets: शंभर (100), दोनशे (200), हजार (1000), लाख (100,000). दीडशे (150) and अडीचशे (250) charm shopkeepers — halves and quarters in pure Marathi. Money talks; count it in Marathi.
topics.title: Counting in Marathi

topics.desc: मी, तुम्ही, हो, नाही — hold your first real Marathi conversations. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: तुमचं नाव काय? (what's your name?) — answer माझं नाव... आहे (my name is...). Names first, friendship follows.
faqs.q: How do I ask someone's name?

faqs.a: हो (yes), नाही (no) — short, clear, universal. होय adds formality; नको means don't-want. Yes-no fluency first.
मला समजलं नाही (I didn't understand) and हळू बोला (please speak slowly). Honesty tunes every speaker to your level.

topics.lede: मी, तुम्ही, हो, नाही — hold your first real Marathi conversations.

links.desc: Dialogues with audio, step by step.
links.label: Marathi conversation lessons

topics.note: A note on मला. मला (mala — to-me) is Marathi's magic word — मला हवं आहे (I want), मला समजलं (I understood), मला माहीत आहे (I know). Experiences flow TOWARD you in Marathi; master मला and fifty sentences unlock.
paras: People anchor talk: मी (I), तुम्ही (you formal), तो (he), ती (she), ते (they). मी मराठी शिकतो/शिकते (I'm learning Marathi) — gender shows on verbs, proudly. Introduce yourself; conversations ignite.
Questions drive dialogue: काय? (what?), कुठे? (where?), कधी? (when?), का? (why?), कसं? (how?). तुम्ही कुठे राहता? (where do you live?) — one question word plus any verb equals conversation.
Politeness oils everything: Marathi says प्लीज (please) and माफ करा (sorry/excuse me). माफ करा, हळू बोला (sorry, speak slowly) — apologies plus requests, the learner's armour.
Repair keeps talk alive: मला समजलं नाही (I didn't understand), पुन्हा सांगा (please say again), याचा अर्थ काय? (what does this mean?). Broken Marathi beats silent perfection — stumble forward daily.
topics.title: Real Marathi conversation

topics.desc: असणे, जाणे, करणे — the verbs that carry every Marathi sentence. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: असणे (to be): मी आहे (I am), तू आहेस, तो/ती आहे, आम्ही आहोत, तुम्ही आहात, ते आहेत. Being first, everything else after.
Three genders show on verbs: जातो (m), जाते (f), जातं (n). Say your gender's ending confidently — मी जातो / मी जाते.
faqs.q: Why do verbs change by gender?

faqs.a: जाणे (to go), येणे (to come), करणे (to do), खाणे (to eat), बोलणे (to speak). Five verbs, half of daily speech.

topics.lede: असणे, जाणे, करणे — the verbs that carry every Marathi sentence.
topics.note: A note on जातो/जाते/जातं. Marathi verbs wear gender openly — मी जातो (I go, male speaker), मी जाते (female), ते जातं (neuter it). Three endings, one verb. Learn your own gender's forms first; the others come through listening.
paras: Being grounds all: असणे (to be) — मी आहे (I am), आम्ही आहोत (we are), तुम्ही आहात (you are), ते आहेत (they are). आहे anchors identity, place, state — मी इथे आहे (I'm here), मी ठीक आहे (I'm fine). Be first.
Going and coming move life: जाणे (to go), येणे (to come) — मी जातो/जाते (I go), मी येतो/येते (I come). Direction verbs plus कुठे (where) navigate Maharashtra — मी मुंबईला जातो (I'm going to Mumbai).
Doing and eating fill days: करणे (to do), खाणे (to eat), पिणे (to drink) — मी काम करतो (I work), मी जेवतो (I eat a meal). Daily verbs, daily use; conjugate them in your sleep.
Speaking and knowing crown all: बोलणे (to speak), वाचणे (to read), लिहिणे (to write) — मी मराठी बोलतो (I speak Marathi). Say it now, imperfectly; say it daily until the mirror agrees.
topics.title: Marathi verbs

topics.desc: पाणी, घर, काम, प्रेम — the hundred words Marathi daily life runs on. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Body, home, food, people: पाणी (water), घर (house), आई (mother), मित्र (friend). Concrete nouns first — point, name, own.
Adjectives agree with gender: चांगला (good-m), चांगली (f), चांगलं (n). Learn triples together — agreement becomes music.
आज (today), उद्या (tomorrow), काल (yesterday), आता (now). Time words frame every plan — learn them this week.

topics.lede: पाणी, घर, काम, प्रेम — the words Marathi daily life runs on.

links.desc: Words in course order, with drills.
links.label: Marathi vocabulary

topics.note: A note on छान. छान (chhaan — nice/great) is Maharashtra's universal praise — छान आहे (it's nice), खूप छान (very nice). Food, films, friends' work — praise everything. Generous छान earns generous friendship.
paras: Survival nouns anchor reality: पाणी (water), अन्न (food), घर (house), रस्ता (road). Point at each, say it aloud, use it today — पाणी हवं आहे (I want water). Concrete first, abstract later.
People words warm speech: माणूस (person), मित्र (friend), आई (mother), मूल (child). माझा मित्र (my friend) introduces proudly; आई calls home. People before things, always.
Describing words add colour: मोठं (big), लहान (small), चांगलं (good), नवीन (new). Adjectives dance with gender — मोठा भाऊ (big brother), मोठी बहीण (big sister). Triple-learn each one.
Time and feeling complete the core: आज (today), प्रेम (love), आनंद (joy), काम (work). आज खूप काम आहे (there's lots of work today) — then प्रेम आणि आनंद balance it. Words for living, not just talking.
topics.title: Core Marathi vocabulary

topics.desc: वडा पाव to पुरणपोळी — order, eat and praise food in Marathi. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: जेवण (meal, esp. lunch/dinner), नाश्ता (breakfast/snacks), चहा (tea). मला भूक लागली (I'm hungry) opens every food conversation.
faqs.q: How do I talk about meals?

faqs.a: हे काय आहे? (what is this?) and मला वडा पाव हवं आहे (I want vada pav). Point, ask, order — menus fear the curious.
तिखट (spicy), गोड (sweet), खारट (salty), आंबट (sour). कमी तिखट (less spicy) saves sensitive tongues.

topics.lede: वडा पाव to पुरणपोळी — order, eat and praise food in Marathi.
topics.note: A note on जेवण. जेवण (jevan — meal) is sacred in Maharashtra — जेवण झालं का? (have you eaten?) is love disguised as a question. Answer हो, झालं (yes, done) and watch faces glow. Food is affection, served hot.
paras: Meals structure the day: नाश्ता (breakfast), जेवण (lunch/dinner), चहा (tea). चहा घेऊया? (shall we have tea?) — Maharashtra runs on cutting chai and conversation. Accept every cup; refuse nothing twice.

Ordering is easy bravery: मला एक चहा हवं आहे (I want one tea), बिल द्या (please give the bill). एक वडा पाव द्या (give one vada pav) — order Mumbai's soul in Marathi. Street vendors reward attempts with extra chutney.

Staples fill the thali: भात (rice), पोळी (flatbread), डाळ (lentils), भाजी (vegetables). भाजी काय आहे? (what's the vegetable dish?) — ask daily, eat variously. Thali eating teaches vocabulary with every bite.

Tastes tune the tongue: तिखट (spicy), गोड (sweet) — पुरणपोळी (sweet stuffed bread) crowns feasts. कमी तिखट करा (make it less spicy) — then खूप छान! (very nice!). Praise the cook; second helpings follow.
topics.title: Food phrases

topics.desc: ळ, nasal vowels, three genders of sound — speak Marathi like a native. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: The retroflex flap: tongue curls back, flaps forward — बाळ (child), शाळा (school). Hindi speakers must learn it fresh; practise flapping daily.
Vowels nasalise before न/म or with चंद्रबिंदु — हवं (want-neuter) hums in speech. Listen for the hum; imitate the music.
Long-short pairs: इ/ई, उ/ऊ change words. Hold long vowels fully double — Marathi ears measure length precisely.

topics.lede: ळ, nasal vowels, rhythm — speak Marathi like a native.
topics.note: A note on हळू. हळू (halu — slowly) is the learner's best friend — हळू बोला (please speak slowly). Say it with a smile and every Marathi speaker shifts to teacher-mode. Slow speech is kind speech; ask for it freely.
paras: The signature ळ rules: बाळ (child), शाळा (school), पोळी (bread) — tongue back, flap forward. Minimal pairs drill it: काळ (time) vs काल (yesterday). Master ळ and Marathis beam; skip it and they still understand, smiling.
Nasals hum through speech: हवं (want) — the चंद्रबिंदु moon-dot nasalises vowels — गावं (villages), पोरं (kids). Hum the vowels; let the nose join the mouth. Music, not mechanics.
Length carries meaning: इ vs ई, उ vs ऊ — short and long are different letters, different words. Double the long ones fully; clip the short ones crisp. Ears measure; mouths must comply.

Rhythm ties it together: हळू (slowly) first, then natural speed; मोठ्याने (loudly) for clarity, शांत (quiet) for calm. उच्चार (pronunciation) improves with echoing — shadow natives daily, record yourself weekly.
topics.title: Marathi pronunciation

topics.desc: Three genders, postpositions, verb-final order — grammar without tears. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Masculine, feminine, neuter — nouns, adjectives AND verbs agree. मोठा/मोठी/मोठं (big), जातो/जाते/जातं (go). Triples everywhere; learn them as sets.
ला marks direction (मुंबईला — to Mumbai), ने marks doers (रामने केलं — Ram did), शी/शी means with. Postpositions follow nouns — learn each with ten examples.
Subject-Object-Verb: मी भात खातो (I rice eat). Verb last, always. English order is the classic beginner error.

topics.lede: Three genders, postpositions, verb-final order — grammar without tears.
topics.note: A note on ला. ला (laa) is Marathi's direction-giver — मुंबईला (to Mumbai), घरी (homeward), मला (to-me). Stick ला on places and people to show movement or feeling-targets. Tiny suffix, enormous workload.
paras: Three genders shape everything: masculine (मुलगा — boy), feminine (मुलगी — girl), neuter (मूल — child, घर — house). Adjectives triple — चांगला/चांगली/चांगलं — and verbs triple too. Gender is not decoration; it is Marathi's skeleton.

Pronouns simplify persons: मी (I), तू (you-informal), तुम्ही (you-formal), तो/ती/ते (he/she/it), आम्ही (we). आम्ही vs आपण (exclusive vs inclusive we) — Marathi distinguishes; English doesn't. Choose your we wisely.

Postpositions replace prepositions: -ला (to), -ने (by/with-instrument), -शी (with-person), -मध्ये (in). मुंबईला जा (go to Mumbai), चमच्याने खा (eat with a spoon). Suffixes after nouns — think backwards from English.

Verbs anchor sentences last: मी भात खातो (I rice eat), ती शाळेत जाते (she to-school goes). Present (खातो), past (खाल्लं), future (खाईन) — tense on verbs, time words framing. Verb-final: the one rule that never breaks.
topics.title: Marathi grammar, plainly explained

topics.desc: Zero to first conversation — your first week of Marathi, step by step. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: नमस्कार, हो, नाही, धन्यवाद, माफ करा, ठीक आहे, मी — seven words that open every door in Maharashtra. Speak them from day one.
faqs.q: What are my first seven words?

faqs.a: No — speak first in Roman letters, add Devanagari in week two. Speakers stay motivated; script-drillers quit. Talk today, read tomorrow.
Twenty focused minutes: five words, one dialogue, one song line. Daily beats marathon — streaks compound into fluency.

topics.lede: Zero to first conversation — your first week of Marathi, step by step.
topics.note: A note on सुरुवात. सुरुवात (survaat — beginning) is the bravest word in Marathi — आजपासून सुरुवात (starting from today). Every fluent speaker once said their first broken नमस्कार. Begin badly; continue daily; arrive surely.
paras: Day one speaks: नमस्कार (hello), हो (yes), नाही (no) — say them to mirrors, pets, shopkeepers. Pronunciation need not be perfect; attempts earn smiles and corrections. Speaking starts speaking; nothing else does.

Days two to four add survival: धन्यवाद (thanks), माफ करा (sorry), पाणी (water), किती? (how much?). Four days, seven words, infinite transactions. Survival Marathi fits in a pocket and works everywhere.

Days five to seven build sentences: मी शिक्षक आहे (I am a teacher), मला चहा हवं आहे (I want tea), तुम्ही कसे आहात? (how are you?). Frames plus words equal conversation — slots fill fast when frames stand ready.

Week two opens the script: अ आ इ ई, then क ख ग घ — Devanagari through familiar words. Read what you already say; letters become friends, not walls. Speak-first learners read faster — motivation decodes.
topics.title: Marathi for absolute beginners

topics.desc: आई, बाबा, आजी, आजोबा — family words that open Marathi homes. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: आई (mother), बाबा (father), भाऊ (brother), बहीण (sister). Family first — Marathis ask about yours within minutes.
काका (uncle), काकू (aunt), आजी (grandmother), आजोबा (grandfather). Extended family, extended vocabulary.
माझं कुटुंब मोठं आहे (my family is big) — माझी आई शिक्षिका आहे (my mother is a teacher). Describe yours; hearts open.
faqs.q: How do I describe my family?

topics.lede: आई, बाबा, आजी, आजोबा — family words that open Marathi homes.
topics.note: A note on आजी. आजी (aaji — grandmother) rules Marathi hearts — आजीच्या गोष्टी (grandmother's stories) raised generations. Learn आजी and आजोबा (grandfather); elders glow when learners speak family. Respect the roots; the tree welcomes you.
paras: Parents anchor all: आई (mother), बाबा (father) — माझी आई (my mother), माझे बाबा (my father). Marathi children chant आई first; learners should too. Home begins here.
Siblings share childhood: भाऊ (brother), बहीण (sister), दादा (elder brother), ताई (elder sister). दादा and ताई mark respect for age — birth order lives in address. Call elders rightly; love follows.

Grandparents crown memory: आजी (grandmother), आजोबा (grandfather) — story-keepers, sweet-givers, wisdom-wells. माझी आजी छान गोष्ट सांगते (my grandmother tells lovely stories) — every Marathi smiles. Honour them in speech.

The household gathers: कुटुंब (family), घर (home), लग्न (wedding), मूल (child). माझं कुटुंब मोठं आहे (my family is big) — then listen; Marathis narrate families with epic joy. Share yours; hear theirs.
topics.title: Family words

topics.desc: किती वाजले? सोमवार to रविवार — time, days and dates in Marathi. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: किती वाजले? (how much has struck?) — answer पाच वाजले (five o'clock). Time strikes in Marathi; ask it everywhere.
faqs.q: How do I ask the time?

faqs.a: सोमवार मंगळवार बुधवार गुरुवार शुक्रवार शनिवार रविवार — chant the week; planet-days roll musically.
आज (today), उद्या (tomorrow), काल (yesterday), परवा (day after/before). Four words frame every plan.

topics.lede: किती वाजले? सोमवार to रविवार — time, days and dates.
topics.note: A note on वाजले. वाजले (vaajale — has struck) makes time musical — किती वाजले? (how much has struck?), पाच वाजले (five has struck). Clocks strike, bells ring, Marathis ask poetically. Time doesn't pass; it chimes.
paras: Clock time strikes: किती वाजले? (what time?), एक वाजला (one o'clock), पाच वाजले (five o'clock). साडेपाच (5:30), पावणेसहा (5:45), सव्वासहा (6:15) — halves and quarters sing. Ask time daily; numbers stick.
Day parts flow: सकाळ (morning), दुपार (afternoon), संध्याकाळ (evening), रात्र (night). सकाळी (in the morning), रात्री (at night) — suffixes time the day. Parts first, precision after.
Weeks cycle planet-wise: सोमवार (Monday) through रविवार (Sunday) — Moon-day to Sun-day. आज सोमवार आहे (today is Monday) — date yourself daily. Weekdays rhythm life.
Dates frame plans: आज (today), उद्या (tomorrow), काल (yesterday), तारीख (date). उद्या भेटूया? (shall we meet tomorrow?) — propose, confirm, arrive. Plans in Marathi keep in Marathi.
topics.title: Time and dates

topics.desc: तिकीट, स्टेशन, कुठे? — travel Maharashtra by train, bus and word. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: रेल्वे स्टेशन कुठे आहे? (where is the railway station?) — swap in बस स्टॉप, विमानतळ. Where-questions navigate nations.
तिकीट किती? (how much is the ticket?) and एक तिकीट द्या (give one ticket). Tickets first, journeys after.
उजवीकडे (right), डावीकडे (left), सरळ (straight). उजवीकडे वळा (turn right) — direct and be directed.

topics.lede: तिकीट, स्टेशन, कुठे? — travel Maharashtra by train, bus and word.
topics.note: A note on प्रवास. प्रवास (pravaas — journey) is Maharashtra's romance — रेल्वे प्रवास (train journey) through the Ghats, monsoon mist on windows. सुखाचा प्रवास (happy journey) blesses every traveller. Journey well; arrive storied.
paras: Stations start journeys: रेल्वे स्टेशन (railway station), बस स्टॉप (bus stop), विमानतळ (airport). स्टेशन कुठे आहे? (where is the station?) — ask anyone; Marathis direct travellers with pride.
Tickets buy passage: तिकीट (ticket) — एक तिकीट द्या (give one ticket), तिकीट किती? (how much?). गाडी कधी येईल? (when will the train come?) — गाडी means both train and car; context steers.
Directions decode cities: उजवीकडे (right), डावीकडे (left), सरळ (straight), जवळ (near), लांब (far). सरळ जा, मग उजवीकडे (go straight, then right) — follow, arrive, thank.
Stays shelter nights: हॉटेल (hotel), खोली (room), पत्ता (address). खोली कितीला? (how much for a room?) — bargain smiling, sleep soundly. प्रवास ends in rest; rest remakes travellers.
topics.title: Travel phrases

topics.desc: किंमत, सूट, रंग — shop in Marathi from first price to final deal. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: याची किंमत काय? (what's the price of this?) — then फक्त किती? (just how much?) for everything else. Two questions, every shop in Maharashtra.
faqs.q: How do I ask the price?

faqs.a: खूप महाग आहे (too costly) with a smile, then थोडं कमी करा (reduce a little). Bargaining is friendly theatre — play your part warmly and the price moves.
Start with five: लाल (red), निळा (blue), हिरवा (green), पिवळा (yellow), पांढरा (white). दुसरा रंग दाखवा (show another colour) reveals the rest.

topics.lede: किंमत, सूट, रंग — shop in Marathi from first price to final deal.

links.label: Marathi shopping

links.desc: Use these lines in real exchanges.
links.label: Marathi conversation lessons

topics.note: A note on थोडं कमी करा. थोडं कमी करा (thodan kami karaa — please reduce a little) is the magic sentence of Maharashtra's markets. Said smiling, it opens every negotiation; said with घेतो (I'll take it) right after, it closes most. Bargaining respects the dance, never the demand.
paras: Prices open every transaction: याची किंमत काय? (what's this one's price?), किती रुपये? (how many rupees?). Listen for the number, repeat it back — पन्नास? (fifty?) — and you are already shopping in Marathi.

Bargaining follows the friendly script: खूप महाग आहे (too costly), सूट द्या (give a discount), थोडं कमी करा (reduce a little). Start walking away slowly — बरं, बघतो (okay, I'll look around) — and the real price often chases you down the street.

Sizes and colours refine the hunt: मोठं द्या (give the big one), लहान द्या (give the small one), नवीन दाखवा (show a new one), दुसरा रंग (another colour). Point, name the change, nod — Marathi shopkeepers read gestures fluently and reward attempts instantly.

Colours close the sale: लाल (red), निळा (blue), हिरवा (green), पिवळा (yellow), पांढरा (white), काळा (black). लाल छान दिसतं (the red looks nice) — then घेतो (I'll take it). Deal done, in Marathi, with a smile on both sides.
topics.title: Shopping and bargaining

topics.desc: मदत, डॉक्टर, रुग्णालय — emergency Marathi you hope to never need. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: मला मदत करा (please help me) — loud, clear, repeated. Add रुग्णालय कुठे आहे? (where is the hospital?) and Marathi crowds mobilise instantly.
faqs.q: What is the one emergency sentence?

faqs.a: Point and say इथे दुखतंय (it hurts here). Then मला बरं वाटत नाही (I feel unwell) and डॉक्टरांना बोलवा (call a doctor). Pain plus pointing crosses every language gap.
हरवलं (it is lost) — पैसे हरवले (money lost), बॅग हरवली (bag lost). Then पोलीस स्टेशन कुठे आहे? (where is the police station?).
faqs.q: How do I report something lost?

topics.lede: मदत, डॉक्टर, रुग्णालय — emergency Marathi you hope to never need.
topics.note: A note on मदत. मदत (madat — help) is Marathi's shortest lifeline — shout it and crowds come running. Maharashtra's bystander culture is famously kind: strangers will escort you to hospitals, translate for doctors, and refuse thanks. Ask loudly; receive gratefully.
paras: The core three save lives: मदत (help), धोका (danger), तातडीची मदत (urgent help). मला मदत करा (please help me) — say it to anyone, anywhere. Marathi crowds respond to distress calls faster than any app; your job is only to ask.

Medical words route the rescue: डॉक्टर (doctor), रुग्णालय (hospital), औषध (medicine), मेडिकल (pharmacy). रुग्णालय कुठे आहे? (where is the hospital?) plus a taxi wave — in cities, help arrives in minutes.

Symptoms speak simply: इथे दुखतंय (it hurts here, point!), मला बरं वाटत नाही (I feel unwell), डोकं दुखतंय (headache), ताप (fever). Pain words plus pointing hands diagnose across every language barrier on earth.

Danger and loss close the kit: आग (fire), चोर (thief), पोलीस (police), हरवलं (it's lost), दूतावास (embassy). Memorise these cold — emergencies never wait for phrasebooks, and ten minutes of drilling buys total peace of mind.
topics.title: Emergency Marathi

topics.desc: तुम्ही or तू? या or ये? Respect levels, decoded with examples. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: तुम्ही for every adult you don't know well — shopkeepers, officials, elders, strangers. तू waits for close friends, children and family. Wrong-side errors embarrass; learners are forgiven, but respect first is always safest.
Use the -ा form: ये becomes या, जा becomes जा, सांग becomes सांगा. One ending, instant politeness — the highest-value sound in Marathi.
faqs.q: How do I make a command polite?

faqs.a: साहेब (sir) and ताई for slightly-older strangers. साहेब, वेळ काय? (sir, what time is it?). Better than pointing and shouting in any language.

topics.lede: तुम्ही or तू? या or ये? Respect levels, decoded.
topics.note: A note on -ा. The -ा ending (aa) is Marathi's respect rocket — या (do come), बघा (please see), सांगा (please tell). One sound that upgrades every request instantly. Stem-alone orders bark; -ा invites.
paras: Marathi has two yous: तुम्ही (formal and plural — strangers, elders, officials) and तू (familiar — friends, children, family). English erased this distinction centuries ago; Marathi keeps it razor-sharp. Every conversation opens with an invisible choice — make it consciously, and make it respectful.

Verbs mirror the split: या (please come) versus ये (come!), सांगा (please say) versus सांग (say!), जा (jaa, please go) versus जा (ja, go — same letters, shorter vowel!). The -ा ending is pure respect — same verb, different universe. Stems bark; -ा invites.

Giving and forgiving show the range: द्या (please give) versus दे (give, familiar), माफ करा (please forgive) versus माफ कर (forgive, familiar). Beggars and kings both hear द्या — politeness in Marathi costs nothing and buys everything.

Strangers get titles: साहेब (sir), दादा (brother), ताई (sister). साहेब, मदत करा (sir, please help) opens any door; barking orders at strangers closes them. Marathi warmth is earned with two syllables of respect.
topics.title: Formal and informal Marathi

topics.desc: Verb-first sentences, मी हवं, नाही vs नको — fix the classic errors. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: English order with Marathi words: मी जा instead of मी जातो, verb first, question words misplaced. Cure: every sentence ends with the verb — practise SOV until English order feels foreign.
faqs.q: What is the most common mistake?

faqs.a: Wanting flows toward people: मला हवं आहे (to-me it-is-wanted), never मी हवं. One of Marathi's deepest patterns — experiences come TO you — and beginners fight it for weeks.
नाही denies facts — पैसे नाहीत (there's no money); नको refuses — नको, धन्यवाद (no thanks, I don't want it). Two no's, two jobs, zero overlap.

topics.lede: Verb-first sentences, मी हवं, नाही vs नको — fix them all.
topics.note: A note on चूक. चूक (chook — mistake) is the kindest word in this lesson — माझी चूक (my mistake) disarms every situation. Marathis adore learners who err boldly and laugh warmly; the only true चूक is silence.
paras: Mistake one: English word order. मी जा (I go — bare stem, wrong) instead of मी जातो (I go — conjugated, right); verbs wandering mid-sentence instead of anchoring the end. Marathi is verb-final, always — SOV is not a suggestion, it is the law.

Mistake two: मी हवं (I want — wrong) instead of मला हवं आहे (to-me wanted — right). Marathi wanting flows toward the wanter; English wanting fires from the wanter. Flip the arrow and dozens of sentences — मला समजलं, मला माहीत आहे — unlock at once.

Mistake three: one-size no. नाही denies facts — पैसे नाहीत (there's no money); नको refuses offers — चहा नको (no tea for me). Beginners spray नाही everywhere; natives smile and correct. Learn both no's, use each precisely.

Mistake four: rushing sounds — flat long vowels, skipped ळ, wrong gender endings. हळू (slowly), बरोबर (correctly), पुन्हा (again): the holy trinity of repair. प्रयत्न (effort) plus सराव (practice) plus संयम (patience) — and अभिनंदन, mistakes become fluency.
topics.title: Mistakes every learner makes

topics.desc: Stop translating in your head — shadowing, thinking aloud and brave first speeches. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Shadow natives: play a Marathi sentence, repeat it aloud half a second behind, matching rhythm and melody. Ten minutes daily rewires your mouth faster than any textbook.
faqs.q: What is the fastest speaking drill?

faqs.a: Yes — narrate your day in Marathi: मी चहा पितो (I'm drinking tea), मी शाळेत जातो. Thinking aloud turns dead time into speaking practice.
faqs.q: Should I talk to myself in Marathi?

faqs.a: Perfectionism. Marathis reward every attempt and correct with love — बोला, चूक हरकत नाही (speak, mistakes are fine). Fluency is corrected mistakes, stacked daily.

topics.note: A note on बोलूया. बोलूया (boluya — let's speak) is permission and invitation in one word — या, मराठीत बोलूया (come, let's speak in Marathi). Say it to every patient listener; doors, hearts and vocabularies open together.
paras: Speaking starts with shadowing: play a Marathi line, echo it half a beat behind, copying music more than words. संभाषण (conversation) is rhythm before grammar — shadow ten minutes daily and your mouth learns Marathi's dance while your brain watches.

Questions and answers volley practice: प्रश्न (question) out, उत्तर (answer) back. Ask yourself everything — हे काय आहे? कुठे? का? — and answer aloud. Self-volleys feel silly for a day, then feel like fluency arriving.

Opinions and stories stretch speeches: मत (opinion), सत्य (truth), गोष्ट (story). माझं मत (in my opinion) forces full sentences; गोष्ट सांग (tell a story) forces sequences. Opinions build sentences; stories build speakers.

Courage closes the circuit: धैर्य (courage) speaks first and perfects later. गाणं (songs) loosen tongues, हसू (laughter) dissolves fear, शांतता (pauses) are allowed. Speak badly today — भाषण (speech) improves only in motion.
topics.title: Speaking practice

topics.desc: Fast speech, films and radio — train your ears until Marathi sounds slow. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Spoken Marathi contracts: जातो melts toward जातोय, करतो toward करतोय. Learn the full forms first, then meet the street forms — this page bridges both.
faqs.q: Why is spoken Marathi so fast?

faqs.a: Children's films and songs first — clear speech, simple stories, endless repetition. Then रेडिओ dramas, then full सिनेमा (cinema). Difficulty ladders beat difficulty cliffs.
faqs.q: What should I listen to first?

faqs.a: Catch the question words — काय, कुठे, कोण, कधी — and the verb at the end. Questions plus verbs carry eighty percent of meaning; the rest is decoration.
faqs.q: How do I catch meaning in fast speech?

topics.note: A note on समजलं का? समजलं का? (samajlan ka — do you understand?) is the kindest question in Marathi — teachers, friends and auto drivers ask it constantly. Answer समजलं (understood) or थोडं थोडं (little by little); honesty tunes every speaker to your level.
paras: Listening begins with attention: लक्ष (attention) — लक्ष देऊन ऐका (listen carefully). Marathi sentences save the verb for last, so ears must hold the whole sentence before meaning lands. Patience is a listening skill; practise holding, not guessing.

Street Marathi contracts beautifully: जातोय, करतोय, बोलतोय — the -तोय ending melts formal -तो. Textbooks teach the full forms; ears must learn the melted ones. Listen for the verb-ghost at sentence end — the meaning hides there.

Media ladders the difficulty: गाणं (songs) first — slow, repetitive, emotional; बातम्या (news) next — clear, formal, standard; रेडिओ (radio) drama third — fast, natural, fun; सिनेमा (films) last — slang, speed, glory. Climb rung by rung; never leap.

Active listening closes the loop: पुन्हा ऐका (listen again), आवाज (sound) by आवाज. Replay each line three times — once for music, once for words, once for meaning. Three passes per line, ten lines per day: ears transform within a month.
topics.title: Understanding spoken Marathi

topics.desc: Words to sentences to stories — reading Marathi from first signs to full pages. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Signboards: दुकान (shop), स्टेशन (station), हॉटेल (restaurant) — big letters, daily repetition, instant rewards. Streets teach faster than textbooks.
Children's books — short वाक्य (sentences), pictures for context, full conjuncts. Then comics, then पेपर headlines, then articles.
faqs.q: When am I ready for books?

faqs.a: Keep a शब्दकोश (dictionary) app open and mine unknown words — five per page, no more. Reading with a dictionary beats studying word lists: context glues memory.
faqs.q: How do I handle unknown words?

topics.lede: Words to sentences to stories — reading Marathi from first signs to full pages.
topics.note: A note on पेपर. Marathi newspapers — लोकसत्ता, सकाळ — use formal written Marathi, nobler than street speech. Headlines first: big type, short lines, daily habit. One headline a day keeps illiteracy away.
paras: Reading starts with words: शब्द (word) by शब्द — वाचा (please read) signs, labels, names. Marathi spelling mirrors speech, so sounding out works: see दुकान, say dukaan, know shop. Phonetic scripts reward beginners richly.

Sentences assemble next: वाक्य (sentence) — subject, object, verb-last. Read SOV sentences end-first for meaning: find the verb, then ask who-did-what. Backwards parsing feels odd for a week, then automatic forever.

Paragraphs and articles follow: परिच्छेद (paragraph), लेख (article), कविता (poem). Children's stories first — short, illustrated, kind — then मासिक (magazines), then साहित्य (literature) itself. Marathi's written heritage spans eight centuries; start at the shallow end.

Dictionaries deepen everything: शब्दकोश (dictionary) — five new words per page, written down, reviewed nightly. Reading without recording entertains; reading with recording teaches. Mine every page; keep every gem.
topics.title: Reading Marathi

topics.desc: Letters to lists to letters — writing Marathi from first strokes to full pages. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Straight headline first: Devanagari letters hang from a top bar — अ, आ, क, म. Rule the line, hang the letters; अक्षर (handwriting) beautifies with mileage.
faqs.q: How do I start writing Marathi?

faqs.a: यादी (lists): shopping lists, word lists, daily plans. Lists forgive grammar, demand spelling, and get used — the perfect beginner writing.
पत्र (letters) to friends, टीप (notes) to self, गृहपाठ (homework) for courses. Real writing to real readers beats copied exercises every time.

topics.lede: Letters to lists to letters — writing Marathi from first strokes to full pages.
topics.note: A note on सही. Your सही (signature) in Devanagari is a milestone — practise it until it flows in one confident motion. Signing Marathi-style on forms, cards and letters declares belonging more than any certificate.
paras: Writing starts with the headline: Devanagari letters hang from a top bar — लिहा (please write) the line first, then hang अ आ इ ई क ख below it. Trace big and slow; the hand learns shapes the eye already knows.
Tools matter little, mileage matters all: पेन (pen), pencil, finger on steamed mirrors — Marathi children trace in notebooks, slates and air. Write everywhere; medium is vanity, motion is learning.

Lists graduate the hand: यादी (list) — टीप (notes), पत्ता (addresses), तारीख (dates). Copy your own नाव (name) fifty times, then friends' names, then street names. Familiar words, fresh script: the fastest fluent hand.

Real writing arrives: पत्र (letters), अर्ज (applications), परीक्षा (exams), गृहपाठ (homework). Write a postcard to yourself in Marathi — short, joyful, posted. First posted Marathi is never forgotten.
topics.title: Writing Marathi

topics.desc: Who does what, verb last — Marathi sentences decoded with living examples. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Subject-Object-Verb: मी पुस्तक वाचतो (I book read). Endings mark roles, so order flexes for emphasis — but verb-last is home.
Tense lives on the verb, with gender: वाचतो/वाचते (read-present), वाचलं (read-past), वाचीन (will read). Time words — काल, आज, उद्या — frame it; the verb carries it.
Add का and rise: हे तुझं पुस्तक आहे का? (is this your book?). Question words — काय, कुठे, कोण — sit where the answer would.

topics.lede: Who does what, verb last — sentences decoded with living examples.
topics.note: A note on पाऊस पडतोय. Marathi weather does things: पाऊस पडतोय (rain is falling), ऊन पडलंय (sun is out), वारा सुटलाय (wind is blowing). No empty it — Marathi skies act. Weather sentences teach SOV with zero confusion: subject, then verb, done.
paras: Simple sentences stack three blocks: मी शाळेत जातो (I — to-school — go), ती गाणं गाते (she — song — sings), आम्ही मराठी शिकतो (we — Marathi — study). Subject, object, verb — build a hundred of these and Marathi skeleton is yours.

Animals make perfect practice: मुलगा हसतो (the boy laughs), कुत्रा भुंकतो (the dog barks), मांजर झोपतं (the cat sleeps). Short subjects, vivid verbs, zero ambiguity — describe every creature you meet and SOV becomes reflex.

Time flexes the frame: मी उद्या येईन (I'll come tomorrow), काल पाऊस पडला (it rained yesterday). Time words float — front for emphasis, middle for flow — while the verb holds the end. Tense plus time word: past, present, future, mastered.

Identity and questions close the set: हे माझं घर आहे (this is my house), हे तुझं पुस्तक आहे का? (is this your book?), सगळं ठीक आहे (all is well). Equate with हे/ते, question with का, reassure with सगळं ठीक आहे — sentences for every situation.
topics.title: Marathi sentence structure

topics.desc: Rahul becomes राहुल — spell, write and own your name in Devanagari. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Sound it out in Devanagari letters: Rahul → राहुल, Priya → प्रिया, John → जॉन. Marathi spells by ear — say your name slowly, catch each sound, write each letter.
faqs.q: How do I write my name in Marathi?

faqs.a: Nukta letters — ज (za), फ (fa) — handle foreign sounds. जॉन (John), फोन (phone) — spotted letters for imported sounds, fully Marathi now.
पहिलं अक्षर (first letter) starts it, शेवटचं अक्षर (last letter) ends it. Introduce with माझं नाव (my name is), then write it — introductions stick twice as well written.
faqs.q: How do I introduce my name?

topics.lede: Rahul becomes राहुल — spell, write and own your name in Devanagari.
topics.note: A note on राहुल. Foreign names glide in Devanagari — Rahul appears as राहुल, sometimes राहूल with a longer vowel. All are read Rahul; none is wrong. Marathi welcomes foreign names with flexible spelling — pick the shape you love and own it.
paras: Names transliterate by ear: break yours into sounds, match each to Devanagari letters — रवी (Ravi), लक्ष्मी (Lakshmi), किरण (Kiran) show the pattern. Say it slow, write it true — स्पेलिंग (spelling) by sound, not by English letters.
Foreign sounds borrow dotted letters: ज for azure-sounds (ॲझर), फ for phone (फोन), ऑ for coffee (कॉफी). These spotted letters are Marathi citizens now — use them proudly for every imported sound.

Introductions pair speech and script: ओळख (introduction) — माझं नाव (my name is), spoken, then written. नावाचे बोर्ड (name boards) on doors and desks teach daily — read every board, collect every name.

Nicknames warm everything: टोपणनाव (nickname) — बाळ (dear child), सोन्या (golden one), पिल्लू (little one). Marathi shortens with love: Ravi becomes रवी, Lakshmi becomes लचू. Earn a Marathi nickname and you have arrived.
topics.title: Write your name in Marathi

topics.desc: भारी, राडा, एक नंबर — street Marathi that films, friends and fun run on. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: भारी (awesome) and एक नंबर (number one) — positive, universal, safe. Sprinkle them on food, films and friends; instant insider status.
भाऊ (bro) and दादा (big bro) — for friends only, never elders or strangers. Friendship slang misused offends; rightly used, it bonds instantly.
Nothing much, just chilling — काय चाललंय? — काई नाई, टाइमपास (what's up? — nothing, timepass). The most Marathi answer in existence: relaxed joy, declared proudly.

topics.lede: भारी, राडा, एक नंबर — street Marathi that fun runs on.
topics.note: A note on टाइमपास. टाइमपास (timepass) defies translation — chilling, hanging out, passing time joyfully. काय करतोयस? — टाइमपास (what are you doing? — timepass). Whole philosophies hide in two syllables; use it freely, smile always.
paras: Praise slang opens doors: भारी (awesome), एक नंबर (number one), लय भारी (very awesome), राडा (rocking), कडक (solid). Food, films, friends' outfits — praise everything loudly. Marathis praise generously; learners should too.

Friendship words bond crews: भाऊ (bro), दादा (big bro), मित्रा (friend) — friends-only, always warm. भाऊ, ये ना (come on bro) starts a thousand conversations daily. Never aim them upward at elders; sideways at friends, fire freely.

Reaction words colour stories: अय्यो (oh no!), अर्रर्र (wow!), गप्प बस (stop making things up, sit quiet!). Marathi storytelling runs on reactions — gasp, laugh, disbelieve theatrically. Flat faces kill stories; big reactions feed them.

Playful edges season everything: चल निघ (get lost — playful among friends, rude otherwise), शी (mild disgust), टाइमपास (chilling). Learn the edges, respect the edges: slang's power is knowing exactly where fun ends.
topics.title: Marathi slang

topics.desc: Toys, moons, stars and good-child gold — Marathi for little learners, big joy. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Songs and गोष्ट (stories) — गाणं with actions, tales with voices. Children absorb Marathi through music and play long before grammar.
faqs.q: How do kids learn Marathi best?

faqs.a: चांगलं मूल (good child) — praise every attempt loudly. Marathi parenting runs on encouragement; learners of all ages bloom under it.
faqs.q: How do I praise a child?

faqs.a: खेळ (games): name objects — चेंडू! खेळणं! — count steps, sing counts. Play first, words hitchhike.

topics.lede: Toys, moons, stars and gold stars — Marathi for little learners, big joy.
topics.note: A note on बाळ. बाळ (baal — baby/darling) melts every Marathi heart — माझं बाळ (my darling) for children, pets and beloveds. Terms of endearment are Marathi's mother tongue; every child swims in them.
paras: Little learners start with love: मुलं (children), बाळ (baby), सोन्या (golden one), चांगलं मूल (good child). Marathi childhood floats on affection-words — call every child बाळ and watch faces light like दिवाळी.
Play teaches fastest: खेळ (play), खेळणं (toy), चेंडू (ball) — खेळूया (let's play)! Count throws, name colours, chase and giggle. Play first; Marathi hitchhikes on joy.
School words structure days: शाळा (school), शिक्षक (teacher), धडा (lesson), गृहपाठ (homework). नमस्कार सर (hello sir) opens every school day — respect and learning, hand in hand.

Sky words spark wonder: सूर्य (sun), चंद्र (moon), तारा (star) — चंद्र बघ (look at the moon)! Night-sky Marathi, whispered on terraces, becomes lifelong memory. Teach the sky; the child keeps the language.
topics.title: Marathi for kids

topics.desc: Meetings, customers, contracts — professional Marathi for offices and business. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: नमस्कार, मी (hello, I'm) — then तुम्हाला भेटून आनंद झाला (pleased to meet you). Business Marathi opens formal and warms slowly.
faqs.q: How do I introduce myself at work?

faqs.a: मीटिंग कधी आहे? (when is the meeting?) and मीटिंग कुठे आहे? (where?). Meetings run Marathi offices — never miss one for language reasons.
faqs.q: How do I ask about meetings?

faqs.a: ईमेल पाठवतो (I'll send an email) and फोनवर बोलूया (let's talk on the phone). Digital Marathi borrows freely — clarity beats purity in business.

topics.lede: Meetings, customers, contracts — professional Marathi for offices.
topics.note: A note on ग्राहक. ग्राहक (graahak — customer) rules Marathi business — ग्राहक हाच राजा (the customer is king). Master it syllable by syllable; clients notice the effort and reward it.
paras: Workplaces run on roles: नोकरी (job), ऑफिस (office), बॉस (boss), ग्राहक (customer), सहकारी (colleague). माझी नोकरी (my job is) introduces your profession; ऑफिस कुठे आहे? finds any office. Roles first, tasks second.

Meetings move business: मीटिंग (meeting), करार (contract/deal), सही (signature). मीटिंग उद्या सकाळी (meeting tomorrow morning) — confirm with ठीक आहे, येतो (okay, I'll come). Marathi meetings open with नमस्कार and close with धन्यवाद.
Money talks plainly: नफा (profit), तोटा (loss), पगार (salary), रजा (leave). पगार कधी होतो? (when is payday?) — asked smiling, everywhere. Business Marathi respects directness wrapped in politeness.
Digital tools connect all: ईमेल (email), फोन (phone), मेसेज (message). ईमेल बघा (please check email) — then यश (success) follows effort. Professional Marathi: formal words, warm heart.
topics.title: Marathi for work and business

topics.desc: Dnyaneshwar, forts, Diwali — reclaim the Marathi your family carried. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Start with sounds you half-know: family words, food names, festival greetings. Heritage ears remember more than they admit — recognition unlocks fast, then production follows.
faqs.q: I understand but can't speak — help?

faqs.a: ज्ञानेश्वर (Dnyaneshwar) — Dnyaneshwari, the Bhagavad-Gita in Marathi verse. Learn one ovi by heart; Marathis of every age will beam.
faqs.q: What is the one classic to know?

faqs.a: दिवाळीच्या शुभेच्छा (Diwali greetings) and गुढीपाडव्याच्या शुभेच्छा (New Year greetings) — festivals are heritage made annual. Greet first, belong instantly.

topics.lede: Dnyaneshwar, forts, Diwali — reclaim the Marathi your family carried.
topics.note: A note on मातृभाषा. मातृभाषा (maatrubhaashaa — mother tongue) is Marathi's most emotional word — language as mother. माझी मातृभाषा मराठी (my mother tongue is Marathi) is identity declared. Heritage learners don't study Marathi; they come home to it.
paras: Heritage starts with recognition: परंपरा (heritage), पूर्वज (ancestors), मातृभाषा (mother tongue), संस्कृती (culture). Words you heard at knees and kitchens — say them now deliberately. Passive memory converts to active speech within weeks of trying.

Forts anchor memory: किल्ला (fort), रायगड (Raigad), शिवाजी महाराज (Shivaji Maharaj). Every heritage family carries fort-Marathi — hill-names, battle-tales, pride-lines. Climb a किल्ला with learning ears; childhood vocabulary resurfaces like monsoon wells.

Festivals calendar the year: दिवाळी (October-November), गुढीपाडवा (New Year, spring), गणपती in full Maharashtra glory. Festival kitchens teach fastest — grind, stir, taste, name everything. Heritage you can eat stays learned.

Classics crown the journey: ज्ञानेश्वर (Dnyaneshwar's ovis), तुकाराम (Tukaram's abhangs), पुणे to मुंबई — महाराष्ट्र entire. One verse memorised outweighs ten lessons completed; heritage learners carry literature, not just language.
topics.title: Marathi for heritage learners

topics.desc: Weeks to chat, months to flow, a year to shine — honest timelines, faster methods. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Survival in 2–4 weeks (greetings, numbers, food), conversation in 3–6 months, comfort in a year — at 20 minutes daily. Consistency beats intensity every time.
faqs.q: How long to hold a conversation?

faqs.a: ळ, nasal vowels, three-gender verbs — जातो, जाते, जातं. Each surrenders to weeks of drilling — this track attacks every one directly.
Daily contact plus weekly speaking: रोज सराव (practise daily), आठवड्यातून बोला (speak weekly). Apps maintain; conversations advance.

topics.lede: Weeks to chat, months to flow, a year to shine — honest Marathi timelines.
topics.note: A note on रोज. रोज (roj — daily, every day) is the whole secret — रोज थोडं (a little every day) beats weekend marathons completely. Streaks compound; Marathi rewards the faithful, not the frantic.
paras: Levels ladder clearly: सुरुवातीची पातळी (beginner — weeks 1–8: survival phrases, core sounds), मध्यम (intermediate — months 3–8: conversations, tenses, reading), प्रगत (advanced — month 9+: films, debates, literature). Each पातळी (level) feels impossible until suddenly it doesn't.

Habits beat hours: रोज (daily) contact, सवय (habit) over heroics. Fifteen minutes of रोज practice — five words, one dialogue, one song line — compounds to fluency while motivation merely visits. Streaks are sacred; protect yours.

Goals steer progress: ध्येय (goal) — सुरुवात (start) with survival, प्रगती (progress) monthly measured. This month: order food. Next: small talk. Then: phone calls. Concrete ध्येय, celebrated loudly — अस्खलितता (fluency) is a trail of kept promises.

Mastery crowns patience: प्रावीण्य (mastery), निश्चय (determination), आत्मविश्वास (confidence). A year of faithful days buys comfortable conversation; two buys belonging. Marathi has waited eight centuries — it will wait for you, and reward you richly.
topics.title: How long does Marathi take?

topics.desc: Indo-Aryan roots, Sanskrit elders, Dravidian neighbours — Marathi's place in India's language family. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Close cousins — Marathi and Hindi are both Indo-Aryan, both Devanagari, sharing thousands of words. Same grandparents, different parents.
हिंदी for daily overlap, गुजराती next door, then संस्कृत above all. The marathi-vs-hindi page maps the closest pair.
faqs.q: Which language is closest to Marathi?

faqs.a: Two millennia of poetry, prayer and scholarship — संस्कृत words fill formal Marathi while grammar stays Prakrit-born. Sanskrit lends vocabulary; Marathi keeps its soul.
faqs.q: Why so much Sanskrit in Marathi?

topics.lede: Indo-Aryan roots, Sanskrit elders, Dravidian neighbours — Marathi's family place.
topics.note: A note on अभिजात. अभिजात (abhijaat — classical) crowns Marathi officially — classical-language status with 2000 years of literature behind it. Dnyaneshwar to Deshpande, unbroken. Classical pride runs deep and joyful; learners inherit the celebration.
paras: Marathi anchors western India: हिंदी (Hindi), गुजराती (Gujarati), बंगाली (Bengali) — cousins, not strangers. Shared Sanskrit roots, shared Devanagari curves, proud separate literatures. Learn Marathi and Hindi signboards start whispering.
The south speaks Dravidian: तमिळ (Tamil), तेलुगू (Telugu), कन्नड (Kannada), मल्याळम (Malayalam) — different family, shared nation: भारत (India) holds both, and भाषांतर (translation) bridges all.

Sanskrit threads everything: संस्कृत lent Marathi thousands of formal words — तत्सम vocabulary crowns speeches and scriptures. Daily speech mixes happily. Both registers are real Marathi; learners need both.

Unity crowns diversity: एकता (unity) — 22 official languages, hundreds of mother tongues, one conversation. Marathis learn Hindi for Delhi, English for globe, Marathi for soul. Every Indian language you meet makes your Marathi richer.
topics.title: Marathi among Indian languages

topics.desc: Cousin languages, shared script — shared words, split sounds, mutual love. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Largely yes for simple speech — घर, पाणी, आई, नाही/नहीं are near-identical. Speed and slang divide them; patience reunites them.
Marathi kept the ळ and three genders; Hindi simplified to two and lost the flap. Cousins with different habits — precisely the words learners say most.
faqs.q: Why do they sound similar yet different?

faqs.a: Marathi first for Maharashtra, Hindi structure second for the nation. Each language halves the other's difficulty — learn one, get the second at a discount.

topics.lede: Cousin languages, shared script — shared words, split sounds.
topics.note: A note on घर = घर. Marathi घर (house) and Hindi घर are the SAME word in the SAME script — thousands work this way. Learn Marathi's core well and Hindi signboards start reading themselves.
paras: The cousins grew side by side: मराठी bloomed in Maharashtra, हिंदी spread across the north. Same Indo-Aryan mother, same Devanagari dress — Marathi kept three genders and ळ while Hindi streamlined to two. History in every sentence.
Shared words delight learners: घर/घर (house), Marathi आई and Hindi माँ differ, but पाणी/पानी (water), घर/घर (house), नाव/नाम (name) overlap enormously. Core vocabulary crosses the border daily.

Split sounds mark the border: Marathi ळ (lla) against Hindi ल, मला (mala — to-me) against मुझे, हो (ho — yes) against हाँ. Pronouns and yes-no drifted most — precisely the words learners say most. Drill the pairs; cross the border daily.

Greetings show both faces: नमस्कार serves both formal while नमस्ते stands Hindi-classic — yet each understands the other's instantly. Cousins recognise cousins; learn either with love and both reward you.
topics.title: Marathi vs Hindi

topics.desc: Dialogues, songs and Natya Sangeet — learn Marathi the cinema way. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Realistic dramas and comedies — clear speech, everyday words, repeatable डायलॉग (dialogues). Marathi cinema's realism teaches natural speech like no textbook.
Watch once with subtitles for story, again pausing to shadow dialogues, songs on loop for sounds. Three passes per film: story, speech, song.
faqs.q: How do I learn from films?

faqs.a: Start with famous lines — short, dramatic, unforgettable. Film dialogues stick like songs; mimicry is fluency's shortcut.

topics.lede: Dialogues, songs and legends — Marathi the cinema way.
topics.note: A note on दादासाहेब फाळके. दादासाहेब फाळके (Dadasaheb Phalke) — father of Indian cinema, a Marathi visionary. Raja Harishchandra (1913) started it all. Film love here is devotion — learn Marathi and you inherit the celebration.
paras: Cinema is Marathi's second classroom: सिनेमा (cinema), थिएटर (theatre), रिलीज (release) — Friday releases are festivals. नट (actors) and नटी (actresses) are family members; दिग्दर्शक (directors) are debated like philosophers. Watch and belong.

Genres teach registers: प्रेम (romance) speaks softly, कॉमेडी (comedy) snaps jokes, ॲक्शन (action) barks orders. Romance first — gentle pace, tender words; comedy second — speed and slang; action last — glory without subtlety.

Dialogues drill memory: डायलॉग (dialogue) — repeat famous lines until they own you. Marathi dialogues are realism with punch; delivering one correctly earns applause from auto drivers to executives. Shadow the stars shamelessly.

Music melts resistance: संगीत (music), गाणं (songs) — learn lyrics line by line, sing them wrong then right. चाहते (fans) sing together; join them. Cinema Marathi is joyful Marathi — and joyful Marathi sticks forever.
topics.title: Learning from Marathi cinema

topics.desc: Friends, lovers, weddings — the Marathi of hearts, spoken truly. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: मित्र (male friend), मैत्रीण (female friend) — then प्रेम (love) and आपुलकी (affection) as bonds deepen. Friendship words first; romance follows naturally.
लग्न (spoken wedding), विवाह (formal wedding) — नवरदेव (groom), नवरी (bride). लग्नाच्या शुभेच्छा (wedding greetings) blesses every couple.
faqs.q: How do I talk about weddings?

faqs.a: माफी (forgiveness) — मला माफ करा (please forgive me), then शांती (peace). Marathi reconciliations run deep and warm; ask sincerely, receive fully.

topics.lede: Friends, lovers, weddings — the Marathi of hearts, spoken truly.
topics.note: A note on प्रेम vs प्रीती. प्रेम (prem) is broad love — family, friends, humanity; प्रीती (preeti) leans romantic. तुमच्या प्रेमासाठी धन्यवाद (thanks for your love) suits everyone; प्रीती belongs to one. Marathi loves precisely.
paras: Friendship opens hearts: मित्र (male friend), मैत्रीण (female friend) — माझा मित्र (my friend) introduces proudly. Marathi friendships run lifelong and deep; मैत्री (friendship) is celebrated in poetry, films and daily chai. Make one Marathi friend and gain a hundred phrases.

Romance speaks softly: प्रियकर (boyfriend), प्रेयसी (girlfriend), प्रेम (love). Marathi romance favours poetry over bluntness — film songs teach the register better than textbooks. Learn gently; speak truly.

Weddings unite families: लग्न (wedding spoken), विवाह (wedding formal), नवरदेव (groom), नवरी (bride). Marathi weddings run for days — music, food, rituals, blessings. लग्नाच्या शुभेच्छा (wedding congratulations) is your ticket to the feast.

Bonds deepen and mend: प्रेम (love), आपुलकी (affection), आयुष्य (life) — माझं आयुष्य (my life) means my beloved. And when bonds strain: माफी (forgiveness), शांती (peace). Marathi hearts forgive spaciously; ask with folded hands.
topics.title: Talking about relationships

topics.desc: Spaced repetition, topic decks, daily streaks — flashcards that actually work. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: पुन्हा पुन्हा (again and again) — but spaced: 1 day, 3 days, 7 days, 30 days. अंतर (spacing) beats cramming; आठवण (memory) loves intervals.
Five to ten per topic — quality over quantity. Master one कार्ड deck fully before opening the next; half-known decks rot.
रोज (daily) short sessions — ten minutes, every day, no exceptions. Streaks compound; विस्मरण (forgetting) loses to routine.

topics.lede: Spaced repetition, topic decks, daily streaks — flashcards that work.
topics.note: A note on उजळणी. उजळणी (ujalani — revision, brushing up) is Marathi's own word for spaced review — recalling again, and again, at widening intervals. The language itself teaches the method: revisit, widen, remember.
paras: Cards carry memory: कार्ड (card) — one word, one side; meaning, the other. आठवण (memory) strengthens with every recall; विस्मरण (forgetting) is just unreviewed memory. Build decks per topic — greetings, food, verbs — and review each separately.

Spacing schedules success: अंतर (interval) — review new cards tomorrow, then in three days, seven, thirty. पुन्हा पुन्हा (again and again), but wider each time. Cramming fills hours; spacing fills years.
Rhythms sustain streaks: रोज (daily) quick decks, आठवड्यातून (weekly) full reviews, महिन्यातून (monthly) championships. Ten daily minutes beat Sunday marathons; streaks turn study into सवय (habit).
Scores gamify growth: गुण (marks), स्पर्धा (contest), यश (achievement) — even अपयश (defeat) teaches. Quiz yourself, beat yesterday's score, celebrate loudly. Flashcards are games that pay in fluency.
topics.title: Flashcards by topic
